heroHeadline: Balikatan 2026 Day 11: 11-Ship Allied Naval Force in West Philippine Sea as PLA Southern Theater Command Launches Scarborough Shoal Combat Patrols; Cebu Activates Full ASEAN Summit Security — 7 Days Out
heroSubtitle: On April 30, 2026 — Day 11 of the largest-ever Balikatan exercise — the AFP and four allied navies deployed 11 warships in the West Philippine Sea for anti-submarine (CASEX), gunnery (GUNNEX), and photographic exercises involving BRP Miguel Malvar, BRP Antonio Luna, USS Ashland, JS Ikazuchi, JS Shimokita, and HMAS Toowoomba, as Chinese vessels shadowed from a distance. The same day, the PLA Southern Theater Command announced 'combat readiness patrols' at Scarborough Shoal (Huangyan Dao) — framed as countermeasures to Balikatan 2026 — while the China Coast Guard ran simultaneous law-enforcement operations in the same waters. The AFP dismissed the PLA's narrative as 'information operations designed to project a false sense of control.' China is now running simultaneous counter-posturing at three axes around the archipelago: east Luzon (Task Group 107, Apr 24-25), north Luzon Strait (naval action group, Apr 28), and west at Scarborough Shoal (Apr 30) — the most layered Chinese military response to a US-Philippines exercise in the post-Cold War era. In Cebu, full readiness was declared for the 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit (May 7-8): the Philippine Coast Guard raised its maritime security alert in Mactan waters, hospitals entered Code Blue, 10,000+ security personnel are deployed, and provincial systems were placed on cybersecurity alert. Seven days remain before leaders arrive. The summit agenda will center on the South China Sea Code of Conduct — which Philippine DFA Secretary Lazaro has called 'something we owe the world' — and Myanmar's contested reintegration.
